The European Union has introduced the EU Kids Act, a legislative proposal aimed at protecting children from the potential harms of social media.

The proposal would introduce age-specific restrictions, including a ban on social media access for children under 12 and supervised “mini accounts” for those aged 13 and 14. For older teenagers, the plan would require platforms to remove or limit features considered addictive.

In Belgium, some schools have already introduced phone bans, with teachers saying the measures have encouraged more interaction among students.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen says the proposed legislation would require major technology companies to implement stronger safety measures. Platforms that fail to comply could face significant fines.

Al Jazeera's Peter Smith reports from Brussels.

The mission also accused Iranian authorities of crimes against humanity during a crackdown on nationwide anti-government protests, citing alleged unlawful killings, torture, arbitrary detention and enforced disappearances.

The findings are based on interviews, satellite imagery, video and other evidence. Both governments have disputed or not publicly responded to the conclusions, while the US has said its military operations comply with the laws of armed conflict.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Thousands of Palestinians in Gaza have suffered life-changing injuries during the war, with children among those most affected. The World Health Organisation says one in four people injured in Gaza since October 2023 has sustained a life-changing injury, with children accounting for up to a quarter of those cases, or around 10,000 children. With medical supplies, prosthetic materials and specialist care in short supply, only about 500 people have received permanent prosthetics. In Khan Younis, a makeshift tent clinic is repairing damaged prostheses and providing temporary support to Palestinians who have struggled to find treatment elsewhere. Prosthetics technician Mohammed al-Khaldi says they repair damaged devices so patients can continue living in difficult conditions inside displacement camps. For many patients, including children, rehabilitation is about more than restoring mobility; it offers hope and a way to rebuild their lives after devastating injuries. 

Al Jazeera's Narges

description: A Syrian military criminal court has sentenced three men over their roles in mass killings along Syria’s coast in March 2025, in the first major test of the new government’s efforts to hold perpetrators accountable for the violence. Two of those sentenced were affiliated with the former Bashar al-Assad regime, while the third was linked to government forces; a fourth defendant was acquitted for lack of evidence. One former regime loyalist received a life sentence for looting and involvement in an illegal armed group, while another was sentenced to death for killing two people and given a life sentence for other offences including looting and inciting violence. A fighter affiliated with government forces received a 20-year sentence for murder.
